   119→// FloorDataGas computes the minimum gas required for a transaction based on its data tokens (EIP-7623).
   120→func FloorDataGas(data []byte) (uint64, error) {
   121→	var (
   122→		z      = uint64(bytes.Count(data, []byte{0}))
   123→		nz     = uint64(len(data)) - z
   124→		tokens = nz*params.TxTokenPerNonZeroByte + z
   125→	)
   126→	// Check for overflow
   127→	if (math.MaxUint64-params.TxGas)/params.TxCostFloorPerToken < tokens {
   128→		return 0, ErrGasUintOverflow
   129→	}
   130→	// Minimum gas required for a transaction based on its data tokens (EIP-7623).
   131→	return params.TxGas + tokens*params.TxCostFloorPerToken, nil
   132→}

   468→func decodeSignature(sig []byte) (r, s, v *big.Int, err error) {
   469→	if len(sig) != crypto.SignatureLength {

   473→	s = new(big.Int).SetBytes(sig[32:64])
   474→	v = new(big.Int).SetBytes([]byte{sig[64] + 27})

   478→func recoverPlain(sighash common.Hash, R, S, Vb *big.Int, homestead bool) (common.Address, error) {

   480→		return common.Address{}, ErrInvalidSig
   481→	}
   482→	V := byte(Vb.Uint64() - 27)
   483→	if !crypto.ValidateSignatureValues(V, R, S, homestead) {
   484→		return common.Address{}, ErrInvalidSig
   485→	}

   487→	r, s := R.Bytes(), S.Bytes()
   488→	sig := make([]byte, crypto.SignatureLength)
   489→	copy(sig[32-len(r):32], r)
   490→	copy(sig[64-len(s):64], s)

   492→	// recover the public key from the signature
   493→	pub, err := crypto.Ecrecover(sighash[:], sig)
   494→	if err != nil {
   495→		return common.Address{}, err
   496→	}
   497→	if len(pub) == 0 || pub[0] != 4 {
   498→		return common.Address{}, errors.New("invalid public key")
   499→	}
   500→	var addr common.Address
   501→	copy(addr[:], crypto.Keccak256(pub[1:])[12:])
   502→	return addr, nil
   503→}

   506→func deriveChainId(v *big.Int) *big.Int {

   182→// modernSigner is the signer implementation that handles non-legacy transaction types.
   183→// For legacy transactions, it defers to one of the legacy signers (frontier, homestead, eip155).
   184→type modernSigner struct {
   185→	txtypes txtypeSet
   186→	chainID *big.Int
   187→	legacy  Signer
   188→}
   189→
   190→// txtypeSet is a bitmap for transaction types.
   191→type txtypeSet [2]uint64
   192→
   193→func (v *txtypeSet) set(txType byte) {
   194→	v[txType/64] |= 1 << (txType % 64)
   195→}
   196→
   197→func (v *txtypeSet) has(txType byte) bool {
   198→	if txType >= byte(len(v)*64) {
   199→		return false
   200→	}
   201→	return v[txType/64]&(1<<(txType%64)) != 0
   202→}
   203→
   204→func newModernSigner(chainID *big.Int, fork forks.Fork) Signer {
   205→	if chainID == nil || chainID.Sign() <= 0 {
   206→		panic(fmt.Sprintf("invalid chainID %v", chainID))
   207→	}
   208→	s := &modernSigner{
   209→		chainID: chainID,
   210→	}
   211→	// configure legacy signer
   212→	switch {
   213→	case fork >= forks.SpuriousDragon:
   214→		s.legacy = NewEIP155Signer(chainID)
   215→	case fork >= forks.Homestead:
   216→		s.legacy = HomesteadSigner{}
   217→	default:
   218→		s.legacy = FrontierSigner{}
   219→	}
   220→	s.txtypes.set(LegacyTxType)
   221→	// configure tx types
   222→	if fork >= forks.Berlin {
   223→		s.txtypes.set(AccessListTxType)
   224→	}
   225→	if fork >= forks.London {
   226→		s.txtypes.set(DynamicFeeTxType)
   227→	}
   228→	if fork >= forks.Cancun {
   229→		s.txtypes.set(BlobTxType)
   230→	}
   231→	if fork >= forks.Prague {
   232→		s.txtypes.set(SetCodeTxType)
   233→	}
   234→	return s
   235→}
   236→
   237→func (s *modernSigner) ChainID() *big.Int {
   238→	return s.chainID
   239→}
   240→
   241→func (s *modernSigner) Equal(s2 Signer) bool {
   242→	other, ok := s2.(*modernSigner)
   243→	return ok && s.chainID.Cmp(other.chainID) == 0 && s.txtypes == other.txtypes && s.legacy.Equal(other.legacy)
   244→}
   245→
   246→func (s *modernSigner) Hash(tx *Transaction) common.Hash {
   247→	return tx.inner.sigHash(s.chainID)
   248→}
   249→
   250→func (s *modernSigner) supportsType(txtype byte) bool {
   251→	return s.txtypes.has(txtype)
   252→}
   253→
   254→func (s *modernSigner) Sender(tx *Transaction) (common.Address, error) {
   255→	tt := tx.Type()
   256→	if !s.supportsType(tt) {
   257→		return common.Address{}, ErrTxTypeNotSupported
   258→	}
   259→	if tt == LegacyTxType {
   260→		return s.legacy.Sender(tx)
   261→	}
   262→	if tx.ChainId().Cmp(s.chainID) != 0 {
   263→		return common.Address{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d want %d", ErrInvalidChainId, tx.ChainId(), s.chainID)
   264→	}
   265→	// 'modern' txs are defined to use 0 and 1 as their recovery
   266→	// id, add 27 to become equivalent to unprotected Homestead signatures.
   267→	V, R, S := tx.RawSignatureValues()
   268→	V = new(big.Int).Add(V, big.NewInt(27))
   269→	return recoverPlain(s.Hash(tx), R, S, V, true)
   270→}
   271→
   272→func (s *modernSigner) SignatureValues(tx *Transaction, sig []byte) (R, S, V *big.Int, err error) {
   273→	tt := tx.Type()
   274→	if !s.supportsType(tt) {
   275→		return nil, nil, nil, ErrTxTypeNotSupported
   276→	}
   277→	if tt == LegacyTxType {
   278→		return s.legacy.SignatureValues(tx, sig)
   279→	}
   280→	// Check that chain ID of tx matches the signer. We also accept ID zero here,
   281→	// because it indicates that the chain ID was not specified in the tx.
   282→	if tx.inner.chainID().Sign() != 0 && tx.inner.chainID().Cmp(s.chainID) != 0 {
   283→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d want %d", ErrInvalidChainId, tx.inner.chainID(), s.chainID)
   284→	}
   285→	R, S, _, err = decodeSignature(sig)
   286→	if err != nil {
   287→		return nil, nil, nil, err
   288→	}
   289→	V = big.NewInt(int64(sig[64]))
   290→	return R, S, V, nil
   291→}

   329→// EIP155Signer implements Signer using the EIP-155 rules. This accepts transactions which
   330→// are replay-protected as well as unprotected homestead transactions.

   332→type EIP155Signer struct {
   333→	chainId, chainIdMul *big.Int
   334→}
   335→
   336→func NewEIP155Signer(chainId *big.Int) EIP155Signer {
   337→	if chainId == nil {
   338→		chainId = new(big.Int)
   339→	}
   340→	return EIP155Signer{
   341→		chainId:    chainId,
   342→		chainIdMul: new(big.Int).Mul(chainId, big.NewInt(2)),

   355→var big8 = big.NewInt(8)
   356→
   357→func (s EIP155Signer) Sender(tx *Transaction) (common.Address, error) {
   358→	if tx.Type() != LegacyTxType {
   359→		return common.Address{}, ErrTxTypeNotSupported
   360→	}
   361→	if !tx.Protected() {
   362→		return HomesteadSigner{}.Sender(tx)

   364→	if tx.ChainId().Cmp(s.chainId) != 0 {

   366→	}
   367→	V, R, S := tx.RawSignatureValues()
   368→	V = new(big.Int).Sub(V, s.chainIdMul)
   369→	V.Sub(V, big8)

   457→func (fs FrontierSigner) Hash(tx *Transaction) common.Hash {

   460→		tx.GasPrice(),
   461→		tx.Gas(),

   468→func decodeSignature(sig []byte) (r, s, v *big.Int, err error) {
   469→	if len(sig) != crypto.SignatureLength {
   470→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("wrong size for signature: got %d, want %d", len(sig), crypto.SignatureLength)
   471→	}
   472→	r = new(big.Int).SetBytes(sig[:32])
   473→	s = new(big.Int).SetBytes(sig[32:64])
   474→	v = new(big.Int).SetBytes([]byte{sig[64] + 27})
   475→	return r, s, v, nil
   476→}
   477→
   478→func recoverPlain(sighash common.Hash, R, S, Vb *big.Int, homestead bool) (common.Address, error) {
   479→	if Vb.BitLen() > 8 {
   480→		return common.Address{}, ErrInvalidSig
   481→	}
   482→	V := byte(Vb.Uint64() - 27)
   483→	if !crypto.ValidateSignatureValues(V, R, S, homestead) {
   484→		return common.Address{}, ErrInvalidSig
   485→	}
   486→	// encode the signature in uncompressed format
   487→	r, s := R.Bytes(), S.Bytes()
   488→	sig := make([]byte, crypto.SignatureLength)
   489→	copy(sig[32-len(r):32], r)
   490→	copy(sig[64-len(s):64], s)
   491→	sig[64] = V
   492→	// recover the public key from the signature
   493→	pub, err := crypto.Ecrecover(sighash[:], sig)
   494→	if err != nil {
   495→		return common.Address{}, err
   496→	}
   497→	if len(pub) == 0 || pub[0] != 4 {
   498→		return common.Address{}, errors.New("invalid public key")
   499→	}
   500→	var addr common.Address
   501→	copy(addr[:], crypto.Keccak256(pub[1:])[12:])
   502→	return addr, nil
   503→}

   505→// deriveChainId derives the chain id from the given v parameter
   506→func deriveChainId(v *big.Int) *big.Int {
   507→	if v.BitLen() <= 64 {
   508→		v := v.Uint64()
   509→		if v == 27 || v == 28 {
   510→			return new(big.Int)
   511→		}
   512→		return new(big.Int).SetUint64((v - 35) / 2)
   513→	}
   514→	vCopy := new(big.Int).Sub(v, big.NewInt(35))
   515→	return vCopy.Rsh(vCopy, 1)
   516→}

    48→// Register adds the engine API to the full node.
    49→func Register(stack *node.Node, backend *eth.Ethereum) error {
    50→	stack.RegisterAPIs([]rpc.API{
    51→		{
    52→			Namespace:     "engine",
    53→			Service:       NewConsensusAPI(backend),
    54→			Authenticated: true,
    55→		},
    56→	})
    57→	return nil
    58→}

    60→const (
    61→	// invalidBlockHitEviction is the number of times an invalid block can be
    62→	// referenced in forkchoice update or new payload before it is attempted
    63→	// to be reprocessed again.
    64→	invalidBlockHitEviction = 128
    65→
    66→	// invalidTipsetsCap is the max number of recent block hashes tracked that
    67→	// have lead to some bad ancestor block. It's just an OOM protection.
    68→	invalidTipsetsCap = 512

    70→	// beaconUpdateStartupTimeout is the time to wait for a beacon client to get

    84→type ConsensusAPI struct {
    85→	eth *eth.Ethereum
    86→
    87→	remoteBlocks *headerQueue  // Cache of remote payloads received
    88→	localBlocks  *payloadQueue // Cache of local payloads generated
    89→
    90→	// The forkchoice update and new payload method require us to return the
    91→	// latest valid hash in an invalid chain. To support that return, we need
    92→	// to track historical bad blocks as well as bad tipsets in case a chain
    93→	// is constantly built on it.
    94→	//
    95→	// There are a few important caveats in this mechanism:
    96→	//   - The bad block tracking is ephemeral, in-memory only. We must never
    97→	//     persist any bad block information to disk as a bug in Geth could end
    98→	//     up blocking a valid chain, even if a later Geth update would accept
    99→	//     it.
   100→	//   - Bad blocks will get forgotten after a certain threshold of import
   101→	//     attempts and will be retried. The rationale is that if the network
   102→	//     really-really-really tries to feed us a block, we should give it a
   103→	//     new chance, perhaps us being racey instead of the block being legit
   104→	//     bad (this happened in Geth at a point with import vs. pending race).
   105→	//   - Tracking all the blocks built on top of the bad one could be a bit
   106→	//     problematic, so we will only track the head chain segment of a bad
   107→	//     chain to allow discarding progressing bad chains and side chains,
   108→	//     without tracking too much bad data.
   109→	invalidBlocksHits map[common.Hash]int           // Ephemeral cache to track invalid blocks and their hit count
   110→	invalidTipsets    map[common.Hash]*types.Header // Ephemeral cache to track invalid tipsets and their bad ancestor
   111→	invalidLock       sync.Mutex                    // Protects the invalid maps from concurrent access
   112→
   113→	// Geth can appear to be stuck or do strange things if the beacon client is
   114→	// offline or is sending us strange data. Stash some update stats away so
   115→	// that we can warn the user and not have them open issues on our tracker.
   116→	lastTransitionUpdate atomic.Int64
   117→	lastForkchoiceUpdate atomic.Int64
   118→	lastNewPayloadUpdate atomic.Int64
   119→
   120→	forkchoiceLock sync.Mutex // Lock for the forkChoiceUpdated method
   121→	newPayloadLock sync.Mutex // Lock for the NewPayload method
   122→}

   124→// NewConsensusAPI creates a new consensus api for the given backend.
   125→// The underlying blockchain needs to have a valid terminal total difficulty set.
   126→//
   127→// This function creates a long-lived object with an attached background thread.
   128→// For testing or other short-term use cases, please use newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat.
   129→func NewConsensusAPI(eth *eth.Ethereum) *ConsensusAPI {
   130→	api := newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat(eth)
   131→	go api.heartbeat()
   132→	return api
   133→}
   134→
   135→// newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat creates a new consensus api for the SimulatedBeacon Node.
   136→func newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat(eth *eth.Ethereum) *ConsensusAPI {
   137→	if eth.BlockChain().Config().TerminalTotalDifficulty == nil {
   138→		log.Warn("Engine API started but chain not configured for merge yet")
   139→	}
   140→	api := &ConsensusAPI{
   141→		eth:               eth,
   142→		remoteBlocks:      newHeaderQueue(),
   143→		localBlocks:       newPayloadQueue(),
   144→		invalidBlocksHits: make(map[common.Hash]int),
   145→		invalidTipsets:    make(map[common.Hash]*types.Header),
   146→	}
   147→	eth.Downloader().SetBadBlockCallback(api.setInvalidAncestor)
   148→	return api
   149→}

   151→// ForkchoiceUpdatedV1 has several responsibilities:
   152→//
   153→// We try to set our blockchain to the headBlock.
   154→//
   155→// If the total difficulty was not reached: we return INVALID.
   156→//
   157→// If the finalizedBlockHash is set: we check if we have the finalizedBlockHash in our db,
   158→// if not we start a sync.
   159→//
   160→// If there are payloadAttributes: we try to assemble a block with the payloadAttributes
   161→// and return its payloadID.
   162→func (api *ConsensusAPI) ForkchoiceUpdatedV1(update engine.ForkchoiceStateV1, payloadAttributes *engine.PayloadAttributes) (engine.ForkChoiceResponse, error) {
   163→	if payloadAttributes != nil {
   164→		switch {
   165→		case payloadAttributes.Withdrawals != nil || payloadAttributes.BeaconRoot != nil:
   166→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, paramsErr("withdrawals and beacon root not supported in V1")
   167→		case !api.checkFork(payloadAttributes.Timestamp, forks.Paris, forks.Shanghai):
   168→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, paramsErr("fcuV1 called post-shanghai")
   169→		}
   170→	}
   171→	return api.forkchoiceUpdated(update, payloadAttributes, engine.PayloadV1, false)
   172→}
   173→
   174→// ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 is equivalent to V1 with the addition of withdrawals in the payload
   175→// attributes. It supports both PayloadAttributesV1 and PayloadAttributesV2.
   176→func (api *ConsensusAPI) ForkchoiceUpdatedV2(update engine.ForkchoiceStateV1, params *engine.PayloadAttributes) (engine.ForkChoiceResponse, error) {
   177→	if params != nil {
   178→		switch {
   179→		case params.BeaconRoot != nil:
   180→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("unexpected beacon root")
   181→		case api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Paris) && params.Withdrawals != nil:
   182→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("withdrawals before shanghai")
   183→		case api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Shanghai) && params.Withdrawals == nil:
   184→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("missing withdrawals")
   185→		case !api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Paris, forks.Shanghai):
   186→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, unsupportedForkErr("fcuV2 must only be called with paris or shanghai payloads")
   187→		}
   188→	}
   189→	return api.forkchoiceUpdated(update, params, engine.PayloadV2, false)
   190→}
   191→
   192→// ForkchoiceUpdatedV3 is equivalent to V2 with the addition of parent beacon block root
   193→// in the payload attributes. It supports only PayloadAttributesV3.
   194→func (api *ConsensusAPI) ForkchoiceUpdatedV3(update engine.ForkchoiceStateV1, params *engine.PayloadAttributes) (engine.ForkChoiceResponse, error) {
   195→	if params != nil {
   196→		switch {
   197→		case params.Withdrawals == nil:
   198→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("missing withdrawals")
   199→		case params.BeaconRoot == nil:
   200→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("missing beacon root")
   201→		case !api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Cancun, forks.Prague, forks.Osaka, forks.BPO1, forks.BPO2, forks.BPO3, forks.BPO4, forks.BPO5):
   202→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, unsupportedForkErr("fcuV3 must only be called for cancun/prague/osaka payloads")
   203→		}
   204→	}
   205→	// TODO(matt): the spec requires that fcu is applied when called on a valid
   206→	// hash, even if params are wrong. To do this we need to split up
   207→	// forkchoiceUpdate into a function that only updates the head and then a
   208→	// function that kicks off block construction.
   209→	return api.forkchoiceUpdated(update, params, engine.PayloadV3, false)
   210→}

   212→func (api *ConsensusAPI) forkchoiceUpdated(update engine.ForkchoiceStateV1, payloadAttributes *engine.PayloadAttributes, payloadVersion engine.PayloadVersion, payloadWitness bool) (engine.ForkChoiceResponse, error) {
   213→	api.forkchoiceLock.Lock()
   214→	defer api.forkchoiceLock.Unlock()
   215→
   216→	log.Trace("Engine API request received", "method", "ForkchoiceUpdated", "head", update.HeadBlockHash, "finalized", update.FinalizedBlockHash, "safe", update.SafeBlockHash)
   217→	if update.HeadBlockHash == (common.Hash{}) {
   218→		log.Warn("Forkchoice requested update to zero hash")
   219→		return engine.STATUS_INVALID, nil // TODO(karalabe): Why does someone send us this?
   220→	}
   221→	// Stash away the last update to warn the user if the beacon client goes offline
   222→	api.lastForkchoiceUpdate.Store(time.Now().Unix())
   223→
   224→	// Check whether we have the block yet in our database or not. If not, we'll
   225→	// need to either trigger a sync, or to reject this forkchoice update for a
   226→	// reason.
   227→	block := api.eth.BlockChain().GetBlockByHash(update.HeadBlockHash)
   228→	if block == nil {
   229→		// If this block was previously invalidated, keep rejecting it here too
   230→		if res := api.checkInvalidAncestor(update.HeadBlockHash, update.HeadBlockHash); res != nil {
   231→			return engine.ForkChoiceResponse{PayloadStatus: *res, PayloadID: nil}, nil
   232→		}
   233→		// If the head hash is unknown (was not given to us in a newPayload request),
   234→		// we cannot resolve the header, so not much to do. This could be extended in
   235→		// the future to resolve from the `eth` network, but it's an unexpected case
   236→		// that should be fixed, not papered over.
   237→		header := api.remoteBlocks.get(update.HeadBlockHash)
   238→		if header == nil {
   239→			log.Warn("Fetching the unknown forkchoice head from network", "hash", update.HeadBlockHash)
   240→			retrievedHead, err := api.eth.Downloader().GetHeader(update.HeadBlockHash)
   241→			if err != nil {
   242→				log.Warn("Could not retrieve unknown head from peers")
   243→				return engine.STATUS_SYNCING, nil
   244→			}
   245→			api.remoteBlocks.put(retrievedHead.Hash(), retrievedHead)
   246→			header = retrievedHead
   247→		}
   248→		// If the finalized hash is known, we can direct the downloader to move
   249→		// potentially more data to the freezer from the get go.
   250→		finalized := api.remoteBlocks.get(update.FinalizedBlockHash)
   251→
   252→		// Header advertised via a past newPayload request. Start syncing to it.
   253→		context := []interface{}{"number", header.Number, "hash", header.Hash()}
   254→		if update.FinalizedBlockHash != (common.Hash{}) {
   255→			if finalized == nil {
   256→				context = append(context, []interface{}{"finalized", "unknown"}...)
   257→			} else {
   258→				context = append(context, []interface{}{"finalized", finalized.Number}...)
   259→			}
   260→		}
   261→		log.Info("Forkchoice requested sync to new head", context...)
   262→		if err := api.eth.Downloader().BeaconSync(header, finalized); err != nil {
   263→			return engine.STATUS_SYNCING, err
   264→		}
   265→		return engine.STATUS_SYNCING, nil
   266→	}
   267→	// Block is known locally, just sanity check that the beacon client does not
   268→	// attempt to push us back to before the merge.
   269→	if block.Difficulty().BitLen() > 0 && block.NumberU64() > 0 {
   270→		ph := api.eth.BlockChain().GetHeader(block.ParentHash(), block.NumberU64()-1)
   271→		if ph == nil {
   272→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, errors.New("parent unavailable for difficulty check")
   273→		}
   274→		if ph.Difficulty.Sign() == 0 && block.Difficulty().Sign() > 0 {
   275→			log.Error("Parent block is already post-ttd", "number", block.NumberU64(), "hash", update.HeadBlockHash, "diff", block.Difficulty(), "age", common.PrettyAge(time.Unix(int64(block.Time()), 0)))
   276→			return engine.ForkChoiceResponse{PayloadStatus: engine.INVALID_TERMINAL_BLOCK, PayloadID: nil}, nil
   277→		}
   278→	}
   279→	valid := func(id *engine.PayloadID) engine.ForkChoiceResponse {
   280→		return engine.ForkChoiceResponse{
   281→			PayloadStatus: engine.PayloadStatusV1{
   282→				Status:          engine.VALID,
   283→				LatestValidHash: &update.HeadBlockHash,
   284→			},
   285→			PayloadID: id,
   286→		}
   287→	}
   288→	if rawdb.ReadCanonicalHash(api.eth.ChainDb(), block.NumberU64()) != update.HeadBlockHash {
   289→		// Block is not canonical, set head.
   290→		if latestValid, err := api.eth.BlockChain().SetCanonical(block); err != nil {
   291→			return engine.ForkChoiceResponse{PayloadStatus: engine.PayloadStatusV1{Status: engine.INVALID, LatestValidHash: &latestValid}}, err
   292→		}
   293→	} else if api.eth.BlockChain().CurrentBlock().Hash() == update.HeadBlockHash {
   294→		// If the specified head matches with our local head, do nothing and keep
   295→		// generating the payload. It's a special corner case that a few slots are
   296→		// missing and we are requested to generate the payload in slot.
   297→	} else {
   298→		// If the head block is already in our canonical chain, the beacon client is
   299→		// probably resyncing. Ignore the update.
   300→		log.Info("Ignoring beacon update to old head", "number", block.NumberU64(), "hash", update.HeadBlockHash, "age", common.PrettyAge(time.Unix(int64(block.Time()), 0)), "have", api.eth.BlockChain().CurrentBlock().Number)
   301→		return valid(nil), nil
   302→	}
   303→	api.eth.SetSynced()
   304→
   305→	// If the beacon client also advertised a finalized block, mark the local
   306→	// chain final and completely in PoS mode.
   307→	if update.FinalizedBlockHash != (common.Hash{}) {
   308→		// If the finalized block is not in our canonical tree, something is wrong
   309→		finalBlock := api.eth.BlockChain().GetBlockByHash(update.FinalizedBlockHash)
   310→		if finalBlock == nil {
   311→			log.Warn("Final block not available in database", "hash", update.FinalizedBlockHash)
   312→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, engine.InvalidForkChoiceState.With(errors.New("final block not available in database"))
   313→		} else if rawdb.ReadCanonicalHash(api.eth.ChainDb(), finalBlock.NumberU64()) != update.FinalizedBlockHash {
   314→			log.Warn("Final block not in canonical chain", "number", finalBlock.NumberU64(), "hash", update.FinalizedBlockHash)
   315→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, engine.InvalidForkChoiceState.With(errors.New("final block not in canonical chain"))
   316→		}
   317→		// Set the finalized block
   318→		api.eth.BlockChain().SetFinalized(finalBlock.Header())
   319→	}
   320→	// Check if the safe block hash is in our canonical tree, if not something is wrong
   321→	if update.SafeBlockHash != (common.Hash{}) {
   322→		safeBlock := api.eth.BlockChain().GetBlockByHash(update.SafeBlockHash)
   323→		if safeBlock == nil {
   324→			log.Warn("Safe block not available in database")
   325→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, engine.InvalidForkChoiceState.With(errors.New("safe block not available in database"))
   326→		}
   327→		if rawdb.ReadCanonicalHash(api.eth.ChainDb(), safeBlock.NumberU64()) != update.SafeBlockHash {
   328→			log.Warn("Safe block not in canonical chain")
   329→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, engine.InvalidForkChoiceState.With(errors.New("safe block not in canonical chain"))
   330→		}
   331→		// Set the safe block
   332→		api.eth.BlockChain().SetSafe(safeBlock.Header())
   333→	}
   334→	// If payload generation was requested, create a new block to be potentially
   335→	// sealed by the beacon client. The payload will be requested later, and we
   336→	// will replace it arbitrarily many times in between.
   337→	if payloadAttributes != nil {
   338→		args := &miner.BuildPayloadArgs{
   339→			Parent:       update.HeadBlockHash,
   340→			Timestamp:    payloadAttributes.Timestamp,
   341→			FeeRecipient: payloadAttributes.SuggestedFeeRecipient,
   342→			Random:       payloadAttributes.Random,
   343→			Withdrawals:  payloadAttributes.Withdrawals,
   344→			BeaconRoot:   payloadAttributes.BeaconRoot,
   345→			Version:      payloadVersion,
   346→		}
   347→		id := args.Id()
   348→		// If we already are busy generating this work, then we do not need
   349→		// to start a second process.
   350→		if api.localBlocks.has(id) {
   351→			return valid(&id), nil
   352→		}
   353→		payload, err := api.eth.Miner().BuildPayload(args, payloadWitness)
   354→		if err != nil {
   355→			log.Error("Failed to build payload", "err", err)
   356→			return valid(nil), engine.InvalidPayloadAttributes.With(err)
   357→		}
   358→		api.localBlocks.put(id, payload)
   359→		return valid(&id), nil
   360→	}
   361→	return valid(nil), nil
   362→}

   364→// ExchangeTransitionConfigurationV1 checks the given configuration against
   365→// the configuration of the node.
   366→func (api *ConsensusAPI) ExchangeTransitionConfigurationV1(config engine.TransitionConfigurationV1) (*engine.TransitionConfigurationV1, error) {
   367→	log.Trace("Engine API request received", "method", "ExchangeTransitionConfiguration", "ttd", config.TerminalTotalDifficulty)
   368→	if config.TerminalTotalDifficulty == nil {
   369→		return nil, errors.New("invalid terminal total difficulty")
   370→	}
   371→	// Stash away the last update to warn the user if the beacon client goes offline
   372→	api.lastTransitionUpdate.Store(time.Now().Unix())
   373→
   374→	ttd := api.config().TerminalTotalDifficulty
   375→	if ttd == nil || ttd.Cmp(config.TerminalTotalDifficulty.ToInt()) != 0 {
   376→		log.Warn("Invalid TTD configured", "geth", ttd, "beacon", config.TerminalTotalDifficulty)
   377→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid ttd: execution %v consensus %v", ttd, config.TerminalTotalDifficulty)
   378→	}
   379→	if config.TerminalBlockHash != (common.Hash{}) {
   380→		if hash := api.eth.BlockChain().GetCanonicalHash(uint64(config.TerminalBlockNumber)); hash == config.TerminalBlockHash {
   381→			return &engine.TransitionConfigurationV1{
   382→				TerminalTotalDifficulty: (*hexutil.Big)(ttd),
   383→				TerminalBlockHash:       config.TerminalBlockHash,
   384→				TerminalBlockNumber:     config.TerminalBlockNumber,
   385→			}, nil
   386→		}
   387→		return nil, errors.New("invalid terminal block hash")
   388→	}
   389→	return &engine.TransitionConfigurationV1{TerminalTotalDifficulty: (*hexutil.Big)(ttd)}, nil

   478→// GetBlobsV1 returns a blob from the transaction pool.
   479→//
   480→// Specification:
   481→//
   482→// Given an array of blob versioned hashes client software MUST respond with an
   483→// array of BlobAndProofV1 objects with matching versioned hashes, respecting the
   484→// order of versioned hashes in the input array.
   485→//
   486→// Client software MUST place responses in the order given in the request, using
   487→// null for any missing blobs. For instance:
   488→//
   489→// if the request is [A_versioned_hash, B_versioned_hash, C_versioned_hash] and
   490→// client software has data for blobs A and C, but doesn't have data for B, the
   491→// response MUST be [A, null, C].
   492→//
   493→// Client software MUST support request sizes of at least 128 blob versioned hashes.
   494→// The client MUST return -38004: Too large request error if the number of requested
   495→// blobs is too large.
   496→//
   497→// Client software MAY return an array of all null entries if syncing or otherwise
   498→// unable to serve blob pool data.
   499→func (api *ConsensusAPI) GetBlobsV1(hashes []common.Hash) ([]*engine.BlobAndProofV1, error) {
   500→	// Reject the request if Osaka has been activated.
   501→	// follow https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/osaka.md#cancun-api
   502→	head := api.eth.BlockChain().CurrentHeader()
   503→	if !api.checkFork(head.Time, forks.Cancun, forks.Prague) {
   504→		return nil, unsupportedForkErr("engine_getBlobsV1 is only available at Cancun/Prague fork")
   505→	}
   506→	if len(hashes) > 128 {
   507→		return nil, engine.TooLargeRequest.With(fmt.Errorf("requested blob count too large: %v", len(hashes)))
   508→	}
   509→	blobs, _, proofs, err := api.eth.BlobTxPool().GetBlobs(hashes, types.BlobSidecarVersion0)
   510→	if err != nil {
   511→		return nil, engine.InvalidParams.With(err)
   512→	}
   513→	res := make([]*engine.BlobAndProofV1, len(hashes))
   514→	for i := 0; i < len(blobs); i++ {
   515→		// Skip the non-existing blob
   516→		if blobs[i] == nil {
   517→			continue
   518→		}
   519→		res[i] = &engine.BlobAndProofV1{
   520→			Blob:  blobs[i][:],
   521→			Proof: proofs[i][0][:],
   522→		}
   523→	}
   524→	return res, nil
   525→}
   526→
   527→// GetBlobsV2 returns a blob from the transaction pool.
   528→//
   529→// Specification:
   530→// Refer to the specification for engine_getBlobsV1 with changes of the following:
   531→//
   532→// Given an array of blob versioned hashes client software MUST respond with an
   533→// array of BlobAndProofV2 objects with matching versioned hashes, respecting
   534→// the order of versioned hashes in the input array.
   535→//
   536→// Client software MUST return null in case of any missing or older version blobs.
   537→// For instance,
   538→//
   539→//   - if the request is [A_versioned_hash, B_versioned_hash, C_versioned_hash] and
   540→//     client software has data for blobs A and C, but doesn't have data for B, the
   541→//     response MUST be null.
   542→//
   543→//   - if the request is [A_versioned_hash_for_blob_with_blob_proof], the response
   544→//     MUST be null as well.
   545→//
   546→// Client software MUST support request sizes of at least 128 blob versioned
   547→// hashes. The client MUST return -38004: Too large request error if the number
   548→// of requested blobs is too large.
   549→//
   550→// Client software MUST return null if syncing or otherwise unable to serve
   551→// blob pool data.
   552→func (api *ConsensusAPI) GetBlobsV2(hashes []common.Hash) ([]*engine.BlobAndProofV2, error) {
   553→	head := api.eth.BlockChain().CurrentHeader()
   554→	if api.config().LatestFork(head.Time) < forks.Osaka {
   555→		return nil, nil
   556→	}
   557→	return api.getBlobs(hashes, true)
   558→}
   559→
   560→// GetBlobsV3 returns a set of blobs from the transaction pool. Same as
   561→// GetBlobsV2, except will return partial responses in case there is a missing
   562→// blob.
   563→func (api *ConsensusAPI) GetBlobsV3(hashes []common.Hash) ([]*engine.BlobAndProofV2, error) {
   564→	head := api.eth.BlockChain().CurrentHeader()
   565→	if api.config().LatestFork(head.Time) < forks.Osaka {
   566→		return nil, nil
   567→	}
   568→	return api.getBlobs(hashes, false)
   569→}
   570→
   571→// getBlobs returns all available blobs. In v2, partial responses are not allowed,
   572→// while v3 supports partial responses.
   573→func (api *ConsensusAPI) getBlobs(hashes []common.Hash, v2 bool) ([]*engine.BlobAndProofV2, error) {
   574→	if len(hashes) > 128 {
   575→		return nil, engine.TooLargeRequest.With(fmt.Errorf("requested blob count too large: %v", len(hashes)))
   576→	}
   577→	available := api.eth.BlobTxPool().AvailableBlobs(hashes)
   578→	getBlobsRequestedCounter.Inc(int64(len(hashes)))
   579→	getBlobsAvailableCounter.Inc(int64(available))
   580→
   581→	// Short circuit if partial response is not allowed
   582→	if v2 && available != len(hashes) {
   583→		getBlobsRequestMiss.Inc(1)
   584→		return nil, nil
   585→	}
   586→	// Retrieve blobs from the pool. This operation is expensive and may involve
   587→	// heavy disk I/O.
   588→	blobs, _, proofs, err := api.eth.BlobTxPool().GetBlobs(hashes, types.BlobSidecarVersion1)
   589→	if err != nil {
   590→		return nil, engine.InvalidParams.With(err)
   591→	}
   592→	// Validate the blobs from the pool and assemble the response
   593→	res := make([]*engine.BlobAndProofV2, len(hashes))
   594→	for i := range blobs {
   595→		// The blob has been evicted since the last AvailableBlobs call.
   596→		// Return null if partial response is not allowed.
   597→		if blobs[i] == nil {
   598→			if !v2 {
   599→				continue
   600→			} else {
   601→				getBlobsRequestMiss.Inc(1)
   602→				return nil, nil
   603→			}
   604→		}
   605→		var cellProofs []hexutil.Bytes
   606→		for _, proof := range proofs[i] {
   607→			cellProofs = append(cellProofs, proof[:])
   608→		}
   609→		res[i] = &engine.BlobAndProofV2{
   610→			Blob:       blobs[i][:],
   611→			CellProofs: cellProofs,
   612→		}
   613→	}
   614→	if len(res) == len(hashes) {
   615→		getBlobsRequestCompleteHit.Inc(1)
   616→	} else if len(res) > 0 {
   617→		getBlobsRequestPartialHit.Inc(1)
   618→	} else {
   619→		getBlobsRequestMiss.Inc(1)
   620→	}
   621→	return res, nil
   622→}

   699→
   700→func (api *ConsensusAPI) newPayload(params engine.ExecutableData, versionedHashes []common.Hash, beaconRoot *common.Hash, requests [][]byte, witness bool) (engine.PayloadStatusV1, error) {
   701→	// The locking here is, strictly, not required. Without these locks, this can happen:
   702→	//
   703→	// 1. NewPayload( execdata-N ) is invoked from the CL. It goes all the way down to
   704→	//      api.eth.BlockChain().InsertBlockWithoutSetHead, where it is blocked on
   705→	//      e.g database compaction.
   706→	// 2. The call times out on the CL layer, which issues another NewPayload (execdata-N) call.
   707→	//    Similarly, this also get stuck on the same place. Importantly, since the
   708→	//    first call has not gone through, the early checks for "do we already have this block"
   709→	//    will all return false.
   710→	// 3. When the db compaction ends, then N calls inserting the same payload are processed
   711→	//    sequentially.
   712→	// Hence, we use a lock here, to be sure that the previous call has finished before we
   713→	// check whether we already have the block locally.
   714→	api.newPayloadLock.Lock()
   715→	defer api.newPayloadLock.Unlock()
   716→
   717→	log.Trace("Engine API request received", "method", "NewPayload", "number", params.Number, "hash", params.BlockHash)
   718→	block, err := engine.ExecutableDataToBlock(params, versionedHashes, beaconRoot, requests)
   719→	if err != nil {
   720→		bgu := "nil"
   721→		if params.BlobGasUsed != nil {
   722→			bgu = strconv.Itoa(int(*params.BlobGasUsed))
   723→		}
   724→		ebg := "nil"
   725→		if params.ExcessBlobGas != nil {
   726→			ebg = strconv.Itoa(int(*params.ExcessBlobGas))
   727→		}
   728→		log.Warn("Invalid NewPayload params",
   729→			"params.Number", params.Number,
   730→			"params.ParentHash", params.ParentHash,
   731→			"params.BlockHash", params.BlockHash,
   732→			"params.StateRoot", params.StateRoot,
   733→			"params.FeeRecipient", params.FeeRecipient,
   734→			"params.LogsBloom", common.PrettyBytes(params.LogsBloom),
   735→			"params.Random", params.Random,
   736→			"params.GasLimit", params.GasLimit,
   737→			"params.GasUsed", params.GasUsed,
   738→			"params.Timestamp", params.Timestamp,
   739→			"params.ExtraData", common.PrettyBytes(params.ExtraData),
   740→			"params.BaseFeePerGas", params.BaseFeePerGas,
   741→			"params.BlobGasUsed", bgu,
   742→			"params.ExcessBlobGas", ebg,
   743→			"len(params.Transactions)", len(params.Transactions),
   744→			"len(params.Withdrawals)", len(params.Withdrawals),
   745→			"beaconRoot", beaconRoot,
   746→			"len(requests)", len(requests),
   747→			"error", err)
   748→		return api.invalid(err, nil), nil
   749→	}
   750→	// Stash away the last update to warn the user if the beacon client goes offline
   751→	api.lastNewPayloadUpdate.Store(time.Now().Unix())
   752→
   753→	// If we already have the block locally, ignore the entire execution and just
   754→	// return a fake success.
   755→	if block := api.eth.BlockChain().GetBlockByHash(params.BlockHash); block != nil {
   756→		log.Warn("Ignoring already known beacon payload", "number", params.Number, "hash", params.BlockHash, "age", common.PrettyAge(time.Unix(int64(block.Time()), 0)))
   757→		hash := block.Hash()
   758→		return engine.PayloadStatusV1{Status: engine.VALID, LatestValidHash: &hash}, nil
   759→	}
   760→	// If this block was rejected previously, keep rejecting it
   761→	if res := api.checkInvalidAncestor(block.Hash(), block.Hash()); res != nil {
   762→		return *res, nil
   763→	}
   764→	// If the parent is missing, we - in theory - could trigger a sync, but that
   765→	// would also entail a reorg. That is problematic if multiple sibling blocks
   766→	// are being fed to us, and even more so, if some semi-distant uncle shortens
   767→	// our live chain. As such, payload execution will not permit reorgs and thus
   768→	// will not trigger a sync cycle. That is fine though, if we get a fork choice
   769→	// update after legit payload executions.
   770→	parent := api.eth.BlockChain().GetBlock(block.ParentHash(), block.NumberU64()-1)
   771→	if parent == nil {
   772→		return api.delayPayloadImport(block), nil
   773→	}
   774→	if block.Time() <= parent.Time() {
   775→		log.Warn("Invalid timestamp", "parent", parent.Time(), "block", block.Time())
   776→		return api.invalid(errors.New("invalid timestamp"), parent.Header()), nil
   777→	}
   778→	// Another corner case: if the node is in snap sync mode, but the CL client
   779→	// tries to make it import a block. That should be denied as pushing something
   780→	// into the database directly will conflict with the assumptions of snap sync
   781→	// that it has an empty db that it can fill itself.
   782→	if api.eth.Downloader().ConfigSyncMode() == ethconfig.SnapSync {
   783→		return api.delayPayloadImport(block), nil
   784→	}
   785→	if !api.eth.BlockChain().HasBlockAndState(block.ParentHash(), block.NumberU64()-1) {
   786→		api.remoteBlocks.put(block.Hash(), block.Header())
   787→		log.Warn("State not available, ignoring new payload")
   788→		return engine.PayloadStatusV1{Status: engine.ACCEPTED}, nil
   789→	}
   790→	log.Trace("Inserting block without sethead", "hash", block.Hash(), "number", block.Number())
   791→	start := time.Now()
   792→	proofs, err := api.eth.BlockChain().InsertBlockWithoutSetHead(block, witness)
   793→	processingTime := time.Since(start)
   794→	if err != nil {
   795→		log.Warn("NewPayload: inserting block failed", "error", err)
   796→
   797→		api.invalidLock.Lock()
   798→		api.invalidBlocksHits[block.Hash()] = 1
   799→		api.invalidTipsets[block.Hash()] = block.Header()
   800→		api.invalidLock.Unlock()
   801→
   802→		return api.invalid(err, parent.Header()), nil
   803→	}
   804→	hash := block.Hash()
   805→
   806→	// Emit NewPayloadEvent for ethstats reporting
   807→	api.eth.BlockChain().SendNewPayloadEvent(core.NewPayloadEvent{
   808→		Hash:           hash,
   809→		Number:         block.NumberU64(),
   810→		ProcessingTime: processingTime,
   811→	})
   812→
   813→	// If witness collection was requested, inject that into the result too
   814→	var ow *hexutil.Bytes
   815→	if proofs != nil {
   816→		ow = new(hexutil.Bytes)
   817→		*ow, _ = rlp.EncodeToBytes(proofs)
   818→	}
   819→	return engine.PayloadStatusV1{Status: engine.VALID, Witness: ow, LatestValidHash: &hash}, nil
   820→}
   821→
   822→// delayPayloadImport stashes the given block away for import at a later time,
   823→// either via a forkchoice update or a sync extension. This method is meant to
   824→// be called by the newpayload command when the block seems to be ok, but some
   825→// prerequisite prevents it from being processed (e.g. no parent, or snap sync).
   826→func (api *ConsensusAPI) delayPayloadImport(block *types.Block) engine.PayloadStatusV1 {
   827→	// Sanity check that this block's parent is not on a previously invalidated
   828→	// chain. If it is, mark the block as invalid too.
   829→	if res := api.checkInvalidAncestor(block.ParentHash(), block.Hash()); res != nil {
   830→		return *res
   831→	}
   832→	// Stash the block away for a potential forced forkchoice update to it
   833→	// at a later time.
   834→	api.remoteBlocks.put(block.Hash(), block.Header())
   835→
   836→	// Although we don't want to trigger a sync, if there is one already in
   837→	// progress, try to extend it with the current payload request to relieve
   838→	// some strain from the forkchoice update.
   839→	err := api.eth.Downloader().BeaconExtend(block.Header())
   840→	if err == nil {
   841→		log.Debug("Payload accepted for sync extension", "number", block.NumberU64(), "hash", block.Hash())
   842→		return engine.PayloadStatusV1{Status: engine.SYNCING}
   843→	}
   844→	// Either no beacon sync was started yet, or it rejected the delivered
   845→	// payload as non-integrate on top of the existing sync. We'll just
   846→	// have to rely on the beacon client to forcefully update the head with
   847→	// a forkchoice update request.
   848→	if api.eth.Downloader().ConfigSyncMode() == ethconfig.FullSync {
   849→		// In full sync mode, failure to import a well-formed block can only mean
   850→		// that the parent state is missing and the syncer rejected extending the
   851→		// current cycle with the new payload.
   852→		log.Warn("Ignoring payload with missing parent", "number", block.NumberU64(), "hash", block.Hash(), "parent", block.ParentHash(), "reason", err)
   853→	} else {
   854→		// In non-full sync mode (i.e. snap sync) all payloads are rejected until
   855→		// snap sync terminates as snap sync relies on direct database injections
   856→		// and cannot afford concurrent out-if-band modifications via imports.

   865→	api.invalidLock.Lock()
   866→	defer api.invalidLock.Unlock()

   872→// checkInvalidAncestor checks whether the specified chain end links to a known
   873→// bad ancestor. If yes, it constructs the payload failure response to return.
   874→func (api *ConsensusAPI) checkInvalidAncestor(check common.Hash, head common.Hash) *engine.PayloadStatusV1 {
   875→	api.invalidLock.Lock()
   876→	defer api.invalidLock.Unlock()
   877→
   878→	// If the hash to check is unknown, return valid
   879→	invalid, ok := api.invalidTipsets[check]
   880→	if !ok {
   881→		return nil
   882→	}
   883→	// If the bad hash was hit too many times, evict it and try to reprocess in
   884→	// the hopes that we have a data race that we can exit out of.
   885→	badHash := invalid.Hash()
   886→
   887→	api.invalidBlocksHits[badHash]++
   888→	if api.invalidBlocksHits[badHash] >= invalidBlockHitEviction {
   889→		log.Error("Too many bad block import attempt, trying", "number", invalid.Number, "hash", badHash)
   890→		delete(api.invalidBlocksHits, badHash)
   891→
   892→		for descendant, badHeader := range api.invalidTipsets {
   893→			if badHeader.Hash() == badHash {
   894→				delete(api.invalidTipsets, descendant)
   895→			}
   896→		}
   897→		return nil
   898→	}
   899→	// Not too many failures yet, mark the head of the invalid chain as invalid
   900→	if check != head {
   901→		log.Warn("Marked new chain head as invalid", "hash", head, "badnumber", invalid.Number, "badhash", badHash)
   902→		for len(api.invalidTipsets) >= invalidTipsetsCap {
   903→			for key := range api.invalidTipsets {
   904→				delete(api.invalidTipsets, key)
   905→				break
   906→			}
   907→		}
   908→		api.invalidTipsets[head] = invalid
   909→	}
   910→	// If the last valid hash is the terminal pow block, return 0x0 for latest valid hash
   911→	lastValid := &invalid.ParentHash
   912→	if header := api.eth.BlockChain().GetHeader(invalid.ParentHash, invalid.Number.Uint64()-1); header != nil && header.Difficulty.Sign() != 0 {
   913→		lastValid = &common.Hash{}
   914→	}
   915→	failure := "links to previously rejected block"
   916→	return &engine.PayloadStatusV1{
   917→		Status:          engine.INVALID,
   918→		LatestValidHash: lastValid,
   919→		ValidationError: &failure,
   920→	}
   921→}

   924→func (api *ConsensusAPI) invalid(err error, latestValid *types.Header) engine.PayloadStatusV1 {
   925→	var currentHash *common.Hash
   926→	if latestValid != nil {

   940→// heartbeat loops indefinitely, and checks if there have been beacon client updates
   941→// received in the last while. If not - or if they but strange ones - it warns the
   942→// user that something might be off with their consensus node.
   943→func (api *ConsensusAPI) heartbeat() {
   944→	// Sleep a bit on startup since there's obviously no beacon client yet
   945→	// attached, so no need to print scary warnings to the user.
   946→	time.Sleep(beaconUpdateStartupTimeout)
   947→
   948→	// If the network is not yet merged/merging, don't bother continuing.
   949→	if api.config().TerminalTotalDifficulty == nil {
   950→		return
   951→	}
   952→
   953→	var offlineLogged time.Time
   954→
   955→	for {
   956→		// Sleep a bit and retrieve the last known consensus updates
   957→		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
   958→
   959→		lastTransitionUpdate := time.Unix(api.lastTransitionUpdate.Load(), 0)
   960→		lastForkchoiceUpdate := time.Unix(api.lastForkchoiceUpdate.Load(), 0)
   961→		lastNewPayloadUpdate := time.Unix(api.lastNewPayloadUpdate.Load(), 0)
   962→
   963→		// If there have been no updates for the past while, warn the user
   964→		// that the beacon client is probably offline
   965→		if time.Since(lastForkchoiceUpdate) <= beaconUpdateConsensusTimeout || time.Since(lastNewPayloadUpdate) <= beaconUpdateConsensusTimeout {
   966→			offlineLogged = time.Time{}
   967→			continue
   968→		}
   969→		if time.Since(offlineLogged) > beaconUpdateWarnFrequency {
   970→			if lastForkchoiceUpdate.IsZero() && lastNewPayloadUpdate.IsZero() {
   971→				if lastTransitionUpdate.IsZero() {
   972→					log.Warn("Post-merge network, but no beacon client seen. Please launch one to follow the chain!")
   973→				} else {
   974→					log.Warn("Beacon client online, but never received consensus updates. Please ensure your beacon client is operational to follow the chain!")
   975→				}
   976→			} else {
   977→				log.Warn("Beacon client online, but no consensus updates received in a while. Please fix your beacon client to follow the chain!")
   978→			}
   979→			offlineLogged = time.Now()
   980→		}
   981→		continue
   982→	}
   983→}

  1067→func (api *ConsensusAPI) getBodiesByRange(start, count hexutil.Uint64) ([]*engine.ExecutionPayloadBody, error) {
  1068→	if start == 0 || count == 0 {
  1069→		return nil, engine.InvalidParams.With(fmt.Errorf("invalid start or count, start: %v count: %v", start, count))
  1070→	}
  1071→	if count > 1024 {
  1072→		return nil, engine.TooLargeRequest.With(fmt.Errorf("requested count too large: %v", count))
  1073→	}
  1074→	// limit count up until current
  1075→	current := api.eth.BlockChain().CurrentBlock().Number.Uint64()
  1076→	last := uint64(start) + uint64(count) - 1
  1077→	if last > current {
  1078→		last = current
  1079→	}
  1080→	bodies := make([]*engine.ExecutionPayloadBody, 0, uint64(count))
  1081→	for i := uint64(start); i <= last; i++ {
  1082→		block := api.eth.BlockChain().GetBlockByNumber(i)
  1083→		bodies = append(bodies, getBody(block))
  1084→	}
  1085→	return bodies, nil
  1086→}

  1088→func getBody(block *types.Block) *engine.ExecutionPayloadBody {
  1089→	if block == nil {
  1090→		return nil
  1091→	}
  1092→
  1093→	var result engine.ExecutionPayloadBody
  1094→
  1095→	result.TransactionData = make([]hexutil.Bytes, len(block.Transactions()))
  1096→	for j, tx := range block.Transactions() {
  1097→		result.TransactionData[j], _ = tx.MarshalBinary()
  1098→	}
  1099→
  1100→	// Post-shanghai withdrawals MUST be set to empty slice instead of nil
  1101→	result.Withdrawals = block.Withdrawals()
  1102→	if block.Withdrawals() == nil && block.Header().WithdrawalsHash != nil {
  1103→		result.Withdrawals = []*types.Withdrawal{}
  1104→	}
  1105→
  1106→	return &result
  1107→}

  1121→// validateRequests checks that requests are ordered by their type and are not empty.
  1122→func validateRequests(requests [][]byte) error {
  1123→	for i, req := range requests {
  1124→		// No empty requests.
  1125→		if len(req) < 2 {
  1126→			return fmt.Errorf("empty request: %v", req)
  1127→		}
  1128→		// Check that requests are ordered by their type.
  1129→		// Each type must appear only once.
  1130→		if i > 0 && req[0] <= requests[i-1][0] {
  1131→			return fmt.Errorf("invalid request order: %v", req)
  1132→		}
  1133→	}
  1134→	return nil
  1135→}

   228→// ExecutableDataToBlock constructs a block from executable data.
   229→// It verifies that the following fields:
   230→//
   231→//		len(extraData) <= 32
   232→//		uncleHash = emptyUncleHash
   233→//		difficulty = 0
   234→//	 	if versionedHashes != nil, versionedHashes match to blob transactions
   235→//
   236→// and that the blockhash of the constructed block matches the parameters. Nil
   237→// Withdrawals value will propagate through the returned block. Empty
   238→// Withdrawals value must be passed via non-nil, length 0 value in data.
   239→func ExecutableDataToBlock(data ExecutableData, versionedHashes []common.Hash, beaconRoot *common.Hash, requests [][]byte) (*types.Block, error) {
   240→	block, err := ExecutableDataToBlockNoHash(data, versionedHashes, beaconRoot, requests)
   241→	if err != nil {
   242→		return nil, err
   243→	}
   244→	if block.Hash() != data.BlockHash {
   245→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("blockhash mismatch, want %x, got %x", data.BlockHash, block.Hash())
   246→	}
   247→	return block, nil
   248→}
   249→
   250→// ExecutableDataToBlockNoHash is analogous to ExecutableDataToBlock, but is used
   251→// for stateless execution, so it skips checking if the executable data hashes to
   252→// the requested hash (stateless has to *compute* the root hash, it's not given).
   253→func ExecutableDataToBlockNoHash(data ExecutableData, versionedHashes []common.Hash, beaconRoot *common.Hash, requests [][]byte) (*types.Block, error) {
   254→	txs, err := decodeTransactions(data.Transactions)
   255→	if err != nil {
   256→		return nil, err
   257→	}
   258→	if len(data.ExtraData) > int(params.MaximumExtraDataSize) {
   259→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid extradata length: %v", len(data.ExtraData))
   260→	}
   261→	if len(data.LogsBloom) != 256 {
   262→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid logsBloom length: %v", len(data.LogsBloom))
   263→	}
   264→	// Check that baseFeePerGas is not negative or too big
   265→	if data.BaseFeePerGas != nil && (data.BaseFeePerGas.Sign() == -1 || data.BaseFeePerGas.BitLen() > 256) {
   266→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid baseFeePerGas: %v", data.BaseFeePerGas)
   267→	}
   268→	var blobHashes = make([]common.Hash, 0, len(txs))
   269→	for _, tx := range txs {
   270→		blobHashes = append(blobHashes, tx.BlobHashes()...)
   271→	}
   272→	if len(blobHashes) != len(versionedHashes) {
   273→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid number of versionedHashes: %v blobHashes: %v", versionedHashes, blobHashes)
   274→	}
   275→	for i := 0; i < len(blobHashes); i++ {
   276→		if blobHashes[i] != versionedHashes[i] {
   277→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid versionedHash at %v: %v blobHashes: %v", i, versionedHashes, blobHashes)
   278→		}
   279→	}
   280→	// Only set withdrawalsRoot if it is non-nil. This allows CLs to use
   281→	// ExecutableData before withdrawals are enabled by marshaling
   282→	// Withdrawals as the json null value.
   283→	var withdrawalsRoot *common.Hash
   284→	if data.Withdrawals != nil {
   285→		h := types.DeriveSha(types.Withdrawals(data.Withdrawals), trie.NewStackTrie(nil))
   286→		withdrawalsRoot = &h
   287→	}
   288→
   289→	var requestsHash *common.Hash
   290→	if requests != nil {
   291→		h := types.CalcRequestsHash(requests)
   292→		requestsHash = &h
   293→	}
   294→
   295→	header := &types.Header{
   296→		ParentHash:       data.ParentHash,
   297→		UncleHash:        types.EmptyUncleHash,
   298→		Coinbase:         data.FeeRecipient,
   299→		Root:             data.StateRoot,
   300→		TxHash:           types.DeriveSha(types.Transactions(txs), trie.NewStackTrie(nil)),
   301→		ReceiptHash:      data.ReceiptsRoot,
   302→		Bloom:            types.BytesToBloom(data.LogsBloom),
   303→		Difficulty:       common.Big0,
   304→		Number:           new(big.Int).SetUint64(data.Number),
   305→		GasLimit:         data.GasLimit,
   306→		GasUsed:          data.GasUsed,
   307→		Time:             data.Timestamp,
   308→		BaseFee:          data.BaseFeePerGas,
   309→		Extra:            data.ExtraData,
   310→		MixDigest:        data.Random,
   311→		WithdrawalsHash:  withdrawalsRoot,
   312→		ExcessBlobGas:    data.ExcessBlobGas,
   313→		BlobGasUsed:      data.BlobGasUsed,
   314→		ParentBeaconRoot: beaconRoot,
   315→		RequestsHash:     requestsHash,
   316→	}
   317→	return types.NewBlockWithHeader(header).
   318→			WithBody(types.Body{Transactions: txs, Uncles: nil, Withdrawals: data.Withdrawals}),
   319→		nil
   320→}

   322→// BlockToExecutableData constructs the ExecutableData structure by filling the
   323→// fields from the given block. It assumes the given block is post-merge block.
   324→func BlockToExecutableData(block *types.Block, fees *big.Int, sidecars []*types.BlobTxSidecar, requests [][]byte) *ExecutionPayloadEnvelope {
   325→	data := &ExecutableData{
   326→		BlockHash:     block.Hash(),
   327→		ParentHash:    block.ParentHash(),
   328→		FeeRecipient:  block.Coinbase(),
   329→		StateRoot:     block.Root(),
   330→		Number:        block.NumberU64(),
   331→		GasLimit:      block.GasLimit(),
   332→		GasUsed:       block.GasUsed(),
   333→		BaseFeePerGas: block.BaseFee(),
   334→		Timestamp:     block.Time(),
   335→		ReceiptsRoot:  block.ReceiptHash(),
   336→		LogsBloom:     block.Bloom().Bytes(),
   337→		Transactions:  encodeTransactions(block.Transactions()),
   338→		Random:        block.MixDigest(),
   339→		ExtraData:     block.Extra(),
   340→		Withdrawals:   block.Withdrawals(),
   341→		BlobGasUsed:   block.BlobGasUsed(),
   342→		ExcessBlobGas: block.ExcessBlobGas(),
   343→	}
   344→
   345→	// Add blobs.
   346→	bundle := BlobsBundle{
   347→		Commitments: make([]hexutil.Bytes, 0),
   348→		Blobs:       make([]hexutil.Bytes, 0),
   349→		Proofs:      make([]hexutil.Bytes, 0),
   350→	}
   351→	for _, sidecar := range sidecars {
   352→		for j := range sidecar.Blobs {
   353→			bundle.Blobs = append(bundle.Blobs, sidecar.Blobs[j][:])
   354→			bundle.Commitments = append(bundle.Commitments, sidecar.Commitments[j][:])
   355→		}
   356→		// - Before the Osaka fork, only version-0 blob transactions should be packed,
   357→		//   with the proof length equal to len(blobs).
   358→		//
   359→		// - After the Osaka fork, only version-1 blob transactions should be packed,
   360→		//   with the proof length equal to CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB * len(blobs).
   361→		//
   362→		// Ideally, length validation should be performed based on the bundle version.
   363→		// In practice, this is unnecessary because blob transaction filtering is
   364→		// already done during payload construction.
   365→		for _, proof := range sidecar.Proofs {
   366→			bundle.Proofs = append(bundle.Proofs, proof[:])
   367→		}
   368→	}
   369→
   370→	return &ExecutionPayloadEnvelope{
   371→		ExecutionPayload: data,
   372→		BlockValue:       fees,
   373→		BlobsBundle:      &bundle,
   374→		Requests:         requests,
   375→		Override:         false,
   376→	}
   377→}

    55→// ValidateTransaction is a helper method to check whether a transaction is valid
    56→// according to the consensus rules, but does not check state-dependent validation

    59→// This check is public to allow different transaction pools to check the basic

    61→func ValidateTransaction(tx *types.Transaction, head *types.Header, signer types.Signer, opts *ValidationOptions) error {

    63→	if opts.Accept&(1<<tx.Type()) == 0 {
    64→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: tx type %v not supported by this pool", core.ErrTxTypeNotSupported, tx.Type())
    65→	}

    67→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: blob count %v, limit %v", ErrTxBlobLimitExceeded, blobCount, opts.MaxBlobCount)

    70→	// smaller than the maximum limit the pool can meaningfully handle
    71→	if tx.Size() > opts.MaxSize {
    72→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: transaction size %v, limit %v", ErrOversizedData, tx.Size(), opts.MaxSize)
    73→	}

   157→// validateBlobTx implements the blob-transaction specific validations.
   158→func validateBlobTx(tx *types.Transaction, head *types.Header, opts *ValidationOptions) error {
   159→	sidecar := tx.BlobTxSidecar()
   160→	if sidecar == nil {
   161→		return errors.New("missing sidecar in blob transaction")
   162→	}
   163→	// Ensure the sidecar is constructed with the correct version, consistent
   164→	// with the current fork.
   165→	version := types.BlobSidecarVersion0
   166→	if opts.Config.IsOsaka(head.Number, head.Time) {
   167→		version = types.BlobSidecarVersion1
   168→	}
   169→	if sidecar.Version != version {
   170→		return fmt.Errorf("unexpected sidecar version, want: %d, got: %d", version, sidecar.Version)
   171→	}
   172→	// Ensure the blob fee cap satisfies the minimum blob gas price
   173→	if tx.BlobGasFeeCapIntCmp(blobTxMinBlobGasPrice) < 0 {
   174→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: blob fee cap %v, minimum needed %v", ErrTxGasPriceTooLow, tx.BlobGasFeeCap(), blobTxMinBlobGasPrice)
   175→	}
   176→	// Ensure the number of items in the blob transaction and various side
   177→	// data match up before doing any expensive validations
   178→	hashes := tx.BlobHashes()
   179→	if len(hashes) == 0 {
   180→		return errors.New("blobless blob transaction")
   181→	}
   182→	if len(hashes) > params.BlobTxMaxBlobs {
   183→		return fmt.Errorf("too many blobs in transaction: have %d, permitted %d", len(hashes), params.BlobTxMaxBlobs)
   184→	}
   185→	if len(sidecar.Blobs) != len(hashes) {
   186→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid number of %d blobs compared to %d blob hashes", len(sidecar.Blobs), len(hashes))
   187→	}
   188→	if err := sidecar.ValidateBlobCommitmentHashes(hashes); err != nil {
   189→		return err
   190→	}
   191→	// Fork-specific sidecar checks, including proof verification.
   192→	if sidecar.Version == types.BlobSidecarVersion1 {
   193→		return validateBlobSidecarOsaka(sidecar, hashes)
   194→	} else {
   195→		return validateBlobSidecarLegacy(sidecar, hashes)
   196→	}
   197→}

   199→func validateBlobSidecarLegacy(sidecar *types.BlobTxSidecar, hashes []common.Hash) error {
   200→	if len(sidecar.Proofs) != len(hashes) {
   201→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid number of %d blob proofs expected %d", len(sidecar.Proofs), len(hashes))
   202→	}
   203→	for i := range sidecar.Blobs {
   204→		if err := kzg4844.VerifyBlobProof(&sidecar.Blobs[i], sidecar.Commitments[i], sidecar.Proofs[i]); err != nil {
   205→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid blob proof: %v", ErrKZGVerificationError, err)
   206→		}
   207→	}
   208→	return nil
   209→}

   211→func validateBlobSidecarOsaka(sidecar *types.BlobTxSidecar, hashes []common.Hash) error {
   212→	if len(sidecar.Proofs) != len(hashes)*kzg4844.CellProofsPerBlob {
   213→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid number of %d blob proofs expected %d", len(sidecar.Proofs), len(hashes)*kzg4844.CellProofsPerBlob)
   214→	}
   215→	if err := kzg4844.VerifyCellProofs(sidecar.Blobs, sidecar.Commitments, sidecar.Proofs); err != nil {
   216→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrKZGVerificationError, err)
   217→	}
   218→	return nil
   219→}

   221→// ValidationOptionsWithState define certain differences between stateful transaction
   222→// validation across the different pools without having to duplicate those checks.
   223→type ValidationOptionsWithState struct {
   224→	State *state.StateDB // State database to check nonces and balances against
   225→
   226→	// FirstNonceGap is an optional callback to retrieve the first nonce gap in
   227→	// the list of pooled transactions of a specific account. If this method is
   228→	// set, nonce gaps will be checked and forbidden. If this method is not set,
   229→	// nonce gaps will be ignored and permitted.
   230→	FirstNonceGap func(addr common.Address) uint64
   231→
   232→	// UsedAndLeftSlots is an optional callback to retrieve the number of tx slots
   233→	// used and the number still permitted for an account. New transactions will
   234→	// be rejected once the number of remaining slots reaches zero.
   235→	UsedAndLeftSlots func(addr common.Address) (int, int)
   236→
   237→	// ExistingExpenditure is a mandatory callback to retrieve the cumulative
   238→	// cost of the already pooled transactions to check for overdrafts.
   239→	ExistingExpenditure func(addr common.Address) *big.Int
   240→
   241→	// ExistingCost is a mandatory callback to retrieve an already pooled
   242→	// transaction's cost with the given nonce to check for overdrafts.
   243→	ExistingCost func(addr common.Address, nonce uint64) *big.Int
   244→}

   246→// ValidateTransactionWithState is a helper method to check whether a transaction
   247→// is valid according to the pool's internal state checks (balance, nonce, gaps).
   248→//
   249→// This check is public to allow different transaction pools to check the stateful
   250→// rules without duplicating code and running the risk of missed updates.
   251→func ValidateTransactionWithState(tx *types.Transaction, signer types.Signer, opts *ValidationOptionsWithState) error {
   252→	// Ensure the transaction adheres to nonce ordering
   253→	from, err := types.Sender(signer, tx) // already validated (and cached), but cleaner to check
   254→	if err != nil {
   255→		log.Error("Transaction sender recovery failed", "err", err)
   256→		return err
   257→	}
   258→	next := opts.State.GetNonce(from)
   259→	if next > tx.Nonce() {
   260→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: next nonce %v, tx nonce %v", core.ErrNonceTooLow, next, tx.Nonce())
   261→	}
   262→	// Ensure the transaction doesn't produce a nonce gap in pools that do not
   263→	// support arbitrary orderings
   264→	if opts.FirstNonceGap != nil {
   265→		if gap := opts.FirstNonceGap(from); gap < tx.Nonce() {
   266→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: tx nonce %v, gapped nonce %v", core.ErrNonceTooHigh, tx.Nonce(), gap)
   267→		}
   268→	}
   269→	// Ensure the transactor has enough funds to cover the transaction costs
   270→	var (
   271→		balance = opts.State.GetBalance(from).ToBig()
   272→		cost    = tx.Cost()
   273→	)
   274→	if balance.Cmp(cost) < 0 {
   275→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: balance %v, tx cost %v, overshot %v", core.ErrInsufficientFunds, balance, cost, new(big.Int).Sub(cost, balance))
   276→	}
   277→	// Ensure the transactor has enough funds to cover for replacements or nonce
   278→	// expansions without overdrafts
   279→	spent := opts.ExistingExpenditure(from)
   280→	if prev := opts.ExistingCost(from, tx.Nonce()); prev != nil {
   281→		bump := new(big.Int).Sub(cost, prev)
   282→		need := new(big.Int).Add(spent, bump)
   283→		if balance.Cmp(need) < 0 {
   284→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: balance %v, queued cost %v, tx bumped %v, overshot %v", core.ErrInsufficientFunds, balance, spent, bump, new(big.Int).Sub(need, balance))
   285→		}
   286→	} else {
   287→		need := new(big.Int).Add(spent, cost)
   288→		if balance.Cmp(need) < 0 {
   289→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: balance %v, queued cost %v, tx cost %v, overshot %v", core.ErrInsufficientFunds, balance, spent, cost, new(big.Int).Sub(need, balance))
   290→		}
   291→		// Transaction takes a new nonce value out of the pool. Ensure it doesn't
   292→		// overflow the number of permitted transactions from a single account
   293→		// (i.e. max cancellable via out-of-bound transaction).
   294→		if opts.UsedAndLeftSlots != nil {
   295→			if used, left := opts.UsedAndLeftSlots(from); left <= 0 {
   296→				return fmt.Errorf("%w: pooled %d txs", ErrAccountLimitExceeded, used)
   297→			}
   298→		}
   299→	}
   300→	return nil
   301→}

    98→// CellProofsAt returns the cell proofs for blob with index idx.
    99→// This method is only valid for sidecars with version 1.
   100→func (sc *BlobTxSidecar) CellProofsAt(idx int) ([]kzg4844.Proof, error) {
   101→	if sc.Version != BlobSidecarVersion1 {
   102→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cell proof unsupported, version: %d", sc.Version)
   103→	}
   104→	if idx < 0 || idx >= len(sc.Blobs) {
   105→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cell proof out of bounds, index: %d, blobs: %d", idx, len(sc.Blobs))
   106→	}
   107→	index := idx * kzg4844.CellProofsPerBlob
   108→	if len(sc.Proofs) < index+kzg4844.CellProofsPerBlob {
   109→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cell proof is corrupted, index: %d, proofs: %d", idx, len(sc.Proofs))
   110→	}
   111→	return sc.Proofs[index : index+kzg4844.CellProofsPerBlob], nil
   112→}

   114→// ToV1 converts the BlobSidecar to version 1, attaching the cell proofs.
   115→func (sc *BlobTxSidecar) ToV1() error {
   116→	if sc.Version == BlobSidecarVersion1 {
   117→		return nil
   118→	}
   119→	if sc.Version == BlobSidecarVersion0 {
   120→		proofs := make([]kzg4844.Proof, 0, len(sc.Blobs)*kzg4844.CellProofsPerBlob)
   121→		for _, blob := range sc.Blobs {
   122→			cellProofs, err := kzg4844.ComputeCellProofs(&blob)
   123→			if err != nil {
   124→				return err
   125→			}
   126→			proofs = append(proofs, cellProofs...)
   127→		}
   128→		sc.Version = BlobSidecarVersion1
   129→		sc.Proofs = proofs
   130→	}
   131→	return nil
   132→}

   134→// encodedSize computes the RLP size of the sidecar elements. This does NOT return the
   135→// encoded size of the BlobTxSidecar, it's just a helper for tx.Size().
   136→func (sc *BlobTxSidecar) encodedSize() uint64 {
   137→	var blobs, commitments, proofs uint64
   138→	for i := range sc.Blobs {
   139→		blobs += rlp.BytesSize(sc.Blobs[i][:])
   140→	}
   141→	for i := range sc.Commitments {
   142→		commitments += rlp.BytesSize(sc.Commitments[i][:])
   143→	}
   144→	for i := range sc.Proofs {
   145→		proofs += rlp.BytesSize(sc.Proofs[i][:])
   146→	}
   147→	return rlp.ListSize(blobs) + rlp.ListSize(commitments) + rlp.ListSize(proofs)
   148→}

   150→// ValidateBlobCommitmentHashes checks whether the given hashes correspond to the
   151→// commitments in the sidecar
   152→func (sc *BlobTxSidecar) ValidateBlobCommitmentHashes(hashes []common.Hash) error {
   153→	if len(sc.Commitments) != len(hashes) {
   154→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid number of %d blob commitments compared to %d blob hashes", len(sc.Commitments), len(hashes))
   155→	}
   156→	hasher := sha256.New()
   157→	for i, vhash := range hashes {
   158→		computed := kzg4844.CalcBlobHashV1(hasher, &sc.Commitments[i])
   159→		if vhash != computed {
   160→			return fmt.Errorf("blob %d: computed hash %#x mismatches transaction one %#x", i, computed, vhash)
   161→		}
   162→	}
   163→	return nil
   164→}

   355→func (tx *BlobTx) decode(input []byte) error {
   356→	// Here we need to support two outer formats: the network protocol encoding of the tx
   357→	// (with blobs) or the canonical encoding without blobs.
   358→	//
   359→	// The canonical encoding is just a list of fields:
   360→	//
   361→	//     [chainID, nonce, ...]
   362→	//
   363→	// The network encoding is a list where the first element is the tx in the canonical encoding,
   364→	// and the remaining elements are the 'sidecar':
   365→	//
   366→	//     [[chainID, nonce, ...], ...]
   367→	//
   368→	// The two outer encodings can be distinguished by checking whether the first element
   369→	// of the input list is itself a list. If it's the canonical encoding, the first
   370→	// element is the chainID, which is a number.
   371→
   372→	firstElem, _, err := rlp.SplitList(input)
   373→	if err != nil {
   374→		return err
   375→	}
   376→	firstElemKind, _, secondElem, err := rlp.Split(firstElem)
   377→	if err != nil {
   378→		return err
   379→	}
   380→	if firstElemKind != rlp.List {
   381→		// Blob tx without blobs.
   382→		return rlp.DecodeBytes(input, tx)
   383→	}
   384→
   385→	// Now we know it's the network encoding with the blob sidecar. Here we again need to
   386→	// support multiple encodings: legacy sidecars (v0) with a blob proof, and versioned
   387→	// sidecars.
   388→	//
   389→	// The legacy encoding is:
   390→	//
   391→	//     [tx, blobs, commitments, proofs]
   392→	//
   393→	// The versioned encoding is:
   394→	//
   395→	//     [tx, version, blobs, ...]
   396→	//
   397→	// We can tell the two apart by checking whether the second element is the version byte.
   398→	// For legacy sidecar the second element is a list of blobs.
   399→
   400→	secondElemKind, _, _, err := rlp.Split(secondElem)
   401→	if err != nil {
   402→		return err
   403→	}
   404→	var payload blobTxWithBlobs
   405→	if secondElemKind == rlp.List {
   406→		// No version byte: blob sidecar v0.
   407→		payload = new(blobTxWithBlobsV0)
   408→	} else {
   409→		// It has a version byte. Decode as v1, version is checked by assign()
   410→		payload = new(blobTxWithBlobsV1)
   411→	}
   412→	if err := rlp.DecodeBytes(input, payload); err != nil {
   413→		return err
   414→	}
   415→	sc := new(BlobTxSidecar)
   416→	if err := payload.assign(sc); err != nil {
   417→		return err
   418→	}
   419→	*tx = *payload.tx()
   420→	tx.Sidecar = sc
   421→	return nil
   422→}

    48→// Register adds the engine API to the full node.
    49→func Register(stack *node.Node, backend *eth.Ethereum) error {
    50→	stack.RegisterAPIs([]rpc.API{
    51→		{
    52→			Namespace:     "engine",
    53→			Service:       NewConsensusAPI(backend),
    54→			Authenticated: true,
    55→		},
    56→	})
    57→	return nil
    58→}

    60→const (
    61→	// invalidBlockHitEviction is the number of times an invalid block can be
    62→	// referenced in forkchoice update or new payload before it is attempted
    63→	// to be reprocessed again.
    64→	invalidBlockHitEviction = 128
    65→
    66→	// invalidTipsetsCap is the max number of recent block hashes tracked that
    67→	// have lead to some bad ancestor block. It's just an OOM protection.
    68→	invalidTipsetsCap = 512

    70→	// beaconUpdateStartupTimeout is the time to wait for a beacon client to get

    84→type ConsensusAPI struct {
    85→	eth *eth.Ethereum
    86→
    87→	remoteBlocks *headerQueue  // Cache of remote payloads received
    88→	localBlocks  *payloadQueue // Cache of local payloads generated
    89→
    90→	// The forkchoice update and new payload method require us to return the
    91→	// latest valid hash in an invalid chain. To support that return, we need
    92→	// to track historical bad blocks as well as bad tipsets in case a chain
    93→	// is constantly built on it.
    94→	//
    95→	// There are a few important caveats in this mechanism:
    96→	//   - The bad block tracking is ephemeral, in-memory only. We must never
    97→	//     persist any bad block information to disk as a bug in Geth could end
    98→	//     up blocking a valid chain, even if a later Geth update would accept
    99→	//     it.
   100→	//   - Bad blocks will get forgotten after a certain threshold of import
   101→	//     attempts and will be retried. The rationale is that if the network
   102→	//     really-really-really tries to feed us a block, we should give it a
   103→	//     new chance, perhaps us being racey instead of the block being legit
   104→	//     bad (this happened in Geth at a point with import vs. pending race).
   105→	//   - Tracking all the blocks built on top of the bad one could be a bit
   106→	//     problematic, so we will only track the head chain segment of a bad
   107→	//     chain to allow discarding progressing bad chains and side chains,
   108→	//     without tracking too much bad data.
   109→	invalidBlocksHits map[common.Hash]int           // Ephemeral cache to track invalid blocks and their hit count
   110→	invalidTipsets    map[common.Hash]*types.Header // Ephemeral cache to track invalid tipsets and their bad ancestor
   111→	invalidLock       sync.Mutex                    // Protects the invalid maps from concurrent access
   112→
   113→	// Geth can appear to be stuck or do strange things if the beacon client is
   114→	// offline or is sending us strange data. Stash some update stats away so
   115→	// that we can warn the user and not have them open issues on our tracker.
   116→	lastTransitionUpdate atomic.Int64
   117→	lastForkchoiceUpdate atomic.Int64
   118→	lastNewPayloadUpdate atomic.Int64
   119→
   120→	forkchoiceLock sync.Mutex // Lock for the forkChoiceUpdated method
   121→	newPayloadLock sync.Mutex // Lock for the NewPayload method
   122→}

   124→// NewConsensusAPI creates a new consensus api for the given backend.
   125→// The underlying blockchain needs to have a valid terminal total difficulty set.
   126→//
   127→// This function creates a long-lived object with an attached background thread.
   128→// For testing or other short-term use cases, please use newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat.
   129→func NewConsensusAPI(eth *eth.Ethereum) *ConsensusAPI {
   130→	api := newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat(eth)
   131→	go api.heartbeat()
   132→	return api
   133→}
   134→
   135→// newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat creates a new consensus api for the SimulatedBeacon Node.
   136→func newConsensusAPIWithoutHeartbeat(eth *eth.Ethereum) *ConsensusAPI {
   137→	if eth.BlockChain().Config().TerminalTotalDifficulty == nil {
   138→		log.Warn("Engine API started but chain not configured for merge yet")
   139→	}
   140→	api := &ConsensusAPI{
   141→		eth:               eth,
   142→		remoteBlocks:      newHeaderQueue(),
   143→		localBlocks:       newPayloadQueue(),
   144→		invalidBlocksHits: make(map[common.Hash]int),
   145→		invalidTipsets:    make(map[common.Hash]*types.Header),
   146→	}
   147→	eth.Downloader().SetBadBlockCallback(api.setInvalidAncestor)
   148→	return api
   149→}

   151→// ForkchoiceUpdatedV1 has several responsibilities:
   152→//
   153→// We try to set our blockchain to the headBlock.
   154→//
   155→// If the total difficulty was not reached: we return INVALID.
   156→//
   157→// If the finalizedBlockHash is set: we check if we have the finalizedBlockHash in our db,
   158→// if not we start a sync.
   159→//
   160→// If there are payloadAttributes: we try to assemble a block with the payloadAttributes
   161→// and return its payloadID.
   162→func (api *ConsensusAPI) ForkchoiceUpdatedV1(update engine.ForkchoiceStateV1, payloadAttributes *engine.PayloadAttributes) (engine.ForkChoiceResponse, error) {
   163→	if payloadAttributes != nil {
   164→		switch {
   165→		case payloadAttributes.Withdrawals != nil || payloadAttributes.BeaconRoot != nil:
   166→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, paramsErr("withdrawals and beacon root not supported in V1")
   167→		case !api.checkFork(payloadAttributes.Timestamp, forks.Paris, forks.Shanghai):
   168→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, paramsErr("fcuV1 called post-shanghai")
   169→		}
   170→	}
   171→	return api.forkchoiceUpdated(update, payloadAttributes, engine.PayloadV1, false)
   172→}
   173→
   174→// ForkchoiceUpdatedV2 is equivalent to V1 with the addition of withdrawals in the payload
   175→// attributes. It supports both PayloadAttributesV1 and PayloadAttributesV2.
   176→func (api *ConsensusAPI) ForkchoiceUpdatedV2(update engine.ForkchoiceStateV1, params *engine.PayloadAttributes) (engine.ForkChoiceResponse, error) {
   177→	if params != nil {
   178→		switch {
   179→		case params.BeaconRoot != nil:
   180→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("unexpected beacon root")
   181→		case api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Paris) && params.Withdrawals != nil:
   182→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("withdrawals before shanghai")
   183→		case api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Shanghai) && params.Withdrawals == nil:
   184→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("missing withdrawals")
   185→		case !api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Paris, forks.Shanghai):
   186→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, unsupportedForkErr("fcuV2 must only be called with paris or shanghai payloads")
   187→		}
   188→	}
   189→	return api.forkchoiceUpdated(update, params, engine.PayloadV2, false)
   190→}
   191→
   192→// ForkchoiceUpdatedV3 is equivalent to V2 with the addition of parent beacon block root
   193→// in the payload attributes. It supports only PayloadAttributesV3.
   194→func (api *ConsensusAPI) ForkchoiceUpdatedV3(update engine.ForkchoiceStateV1, params *engine.PayloadAttributes) (engine.ForkChoiceResponse, error) {
   195→	if params != nil {
   196→		switch {
   197→		case params.Withdrawals == nil:
   198→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("missing withdrawals")
   199→		case params.BeaconRoot == nil:
   200→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, attributesErr("missing beacon root")
   201→		case !api.checkFork(params.Timestamp, forks.Cancun, forks.Prague, forks.Osaka, forks.BPO1, forks.BPO2, forks.BPO3, forks.BPO4, forks.BPO5):
   202→			return engine.STATUS_INVALID, unsupportedForkErr("fcuV3 must only be called for cancun/prague/osaka payloads")
   203→		}
   204→	}
   205→	// TODO(matt): the spec requires that fcu is applied when called on a valid
   206→	// hash, even if params are wrong. To do this we need to split up
   207→	// forkchoiceUpdate into a function that only updates the head and then a
   208→	// function that kicks off block construction.
   209→	return api.forkchoiceUpdated(update, params, engine.PayloadV3, false)
   210→}
